Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)

runners_data.name: Supreme Lord
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win over 6f good ground in latest start and strong 4/4 record on similar going — Donagh O'Connor booking is workmanlike, and 9 days' freshness is ideal; sits directly behind Lady Patrona and needs clean passage at the 2f pole.
runners_data.comment: Supreme Lord won last time out and, returning fit on just nine days' rest, has experience of today's trip and conditions; the 139 lb burden is the one query, but his recent winning form makes him the pick of the field.

runners_data.name: La Tache
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for G M Lyons, which is a significant stable and jockey upgrade worth noting, but 43 days off the track is a concern and her 6f form (two fourth-place finishes) is shakier than her 5f figures; wears a hood and will want to race prominently, adding to congestion.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, La Tache arrives at draw eight carrying 138 lb on a compact 43-day break; the main risk is that he was beaten into fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type ridden by the 3lb claimer Paddy Harnett for the Donnacha O'Brien yard; six runs of consistent placing form over 5-7f on good ground are encouraging, though her only wins have not come at this trip — she needs others to burn bright early.

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Won over 6f good on good ground two starts ago and has 5/6 course-trip form on similar going, making her one of the more course-proven prominent types in this field; Reese Holohan (7lb claim) is an economy jockey option for the yard, and 20 days between runs is a comfortable return.
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time out and was a winner three starts back, so I Ready arrives in fair nick after a 20-day break, with both distance and going experience in his locker; the 132 lb burden and a mid-table rating of 84 are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid placing record over 5-6f on good, trained by the smaller Mulvany yard and ridden by 3lb claimer Wesley Joyce; ran just 5 days ago which is an obvious concern for fatigue, and he has yet to win — he needs others to oblige in front.
runners_data.comment: Lars Soldier shaped with promise when second three starts back and third five starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid grounding; the concern is he has been winless in recent starts and at 131 lb faces a stiff task on just five days' rest.

runners_data.name: Lady Patrona
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner in this field — her latest win over 6f good at Navan for the Harrington yard with Shane Foley aboard ticks every box, and 4/4 on similar going underpins her going profile; the key risk is whether the congested prominent group can organise quickly enough to apply pressure in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Lady Patrona arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, while her rating of 93 puts her clear at the head of this field — the chief worry is whether 129 lb from stall one blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Shesthedevil
runners_data.note: A hold-up type whose sole win came over 6f good ground two starts ago; Patrick Magee's yard has a quiet recent strike rate and Chris Hayes is a solid jockey without a strong tactical advantage from the rear — she needs Lady Patrona to exhaust the prominent group.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive sixth-place finishes make Shesthedevil hard to fancy on recent form, and our figures rank her towards the foot of this field, though she does hold a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh rides this hold-up type who won over 6f good ground two starts ago and has 5/5 going-form consistency — wore a hood (p) previously; the Davison yard has a quiet 14-day strike rate but the horse's form progression is the most encouraging of the genuine closers.
runners_data.comment: Howlin Wolf showed his best when winning two starts back, though he was only fourth and seventh in earlier starts before bouncing back into second last time out; he has distance and going experience to draw on, but his speed rating of 61 and ranking seventh of ten suggest he faces a stiff ask from stall three carrying 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh sends out this 2yo whose entire form profile is back-of-field finishes (four eighth-places over 5-6f good) — a true hold-up type whose redistribution forward in the map overstates her positional options; STYLE_FIT discount applies and there is little in the bare form to suggest a breakthrough here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with three finishes of seventh or worse in that sequence, Celestial Crown is hard to fancy from stall seven carrying 119 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and that familiarity offers modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Captain James Cook
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides this Aidan O'Brien-trained 2yo who is a natural front-runner but whose three-run form (6th, 7th, 12th over 6-8f good) offers little encouragement — redistributed to midfield in the map because the pace positions are taken, meaning he is forced to race away from his preferred role; STYLE_FIT tempers confidence significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Captain James Cook faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and 18 days between runs leaves him fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Patrona is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Shane Foley aboard for the Harrington yard, she is likely to slot into an uncontested lead and control tempo at a measured, sustainable gallop on good ground at Navan. Behind her, Supreme Lord, La Tache, I Ready, and Lars Soldier all want to race prominently, creating a congested second rank from the gate — that four-way squeeze for the two or three available prominent slots is the primary danger zone between the 2f and 3f markers. The field holds more pace-hungry types than the map can accommodate, with Captain James Cook — a genuine front-runner by nature — almost certain to be shuffled back into midfield, while Celestial Crown, a true hold-up horse, is similarly unlikely to find its ideal rearward berth in a field this busy. This race shape, with one controlled front-runner and a bunched prominent group immediately behind, strongly favours horses who can race in the first two or three lengths of the leader and sustain their effort through the final furlong — a settled prominent profile, rather than deep closers forced to find room late, is the type the shape rewards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Patrona Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Patrona finds an uncontested lead and the prominent pack fails to apply sustained pressure, allowing her to dictate a fair but not frantic gallop.
scenarios.body: Lady Patrona's recent win over this course and distance on good ground underlines her aptitude for exactly these conditions, and with no rival willing or able to push up and challenge her, she can conserve energy through the middle and quicken off her own pace in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Presser Runs Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If one of the organised prominent runners — Supreme Lord or I Ready — tracks Lady Patrona in a clear second position and finds a length or two better turning for home.
scenarios.body: With the prominent group congested rather than stretched, the horse that secures the cleanest rail berth and a clear line of running past the 2f pole is best placed to run Lady Patrona down inside the final furlong; Supreme Lord's recent win over 6f on good ground and I Ready's course-distance winning form make them the two most credible dangers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group sets a stronger pace than expected through the first three furlongs, burning off their own stamina and leaving a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Tradewinds, who has shown consistent placing form over 6f on good ground, and Howlin Wolf, who has won over this trip on similar going, are the two genuine hold-up types capable of exploiting a weakening prominent group if gaps materialise inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Handicap Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the early three-way jostle for prominent positions causes interference or a stumble that disrupts Lady Patrona's stride and scrambles the field order entering the straight.
scenarios.body: This unlikely but not impossible scenario benefits whichever lightly-raced or lower-rated horse finds a clean passage through the chaos — Captain James Cook and Celestial Crown, though racing out of their natural roles, are the only runners low enough in the weights to capitalise on a fluke-driven situation at long odds.

watchPoints.text: Lady Patrona must find a clean break from the gate — if she is slow away, Supreme Lord or I Ready could steal the rail and deny her the uncontested lead that the entire pace narrative depends on.

The cluster of Supreme Lord, La Tache, I Ready, and Lars Soldier all wanting to race prominently creates a high-risk squeeze between the 2f and 3f marks — any bumping or checking there could knock the form analysis sideways.

La Tache has been off 43 days and wears a hood — Colin Keane's presence lifts her market profile, but rustiness at 6f (two fourths in form) means she could run too free in the congested prominent group and burn out.

Howlin Wolf and Tradewinds are the only runners whose scenario genuinely requires Lady Patrona to have set a strong enough gallop to bring them into play — watch the early sectional to judge whether the pace is fast enough to suit genuine hold-up types.

Captain James Cook (Lordan/O'Brien) is worth tracking for market moves given the powerful connections, but his redistribution out of his natural front-running role and three blank efforts in form mean any support deserves scrutiny rather than automatic respect.

runners_data.name: Agostino
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer 281 days absent — the layoff is a serious flag at OR=59 in a competitive 19-runner sprint, and his recent Good-ground record (0 wins, 0 places from 15 sim-going runs) offers little encouragement for a fresh return.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 281 days, Agostino faces a stiff task here, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; carrying 142 lb from stall 10 and rated just 59, he has experience over today's trip and going but must prove his layoff hasn't blunted him.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Runs on Good ground exclusively and has five placed efforts in similar conditions, but her hold-up style is a genuine liability in a 19-runner 5f where gaps may not materialise in time.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second five starts back, Irish Rumour arrives here fit on a 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 65 gives her a case despite carrying 142 lb from stall 14 while yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by Charles Weld with five recent runs on Good ground, including two runner-up efforts over 6f — stepping back to 5f is the question, but Shane Foley's booking gives the yard confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Rosato does bring second-place finishes two and four starts back to suggest she can hit the frame, though unplaced efforts either side temper expectations; she has run over today's trip and going before and runs fresh off a seven-day turnaround carrying 142 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Surpass And Shine
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two 5f wins on Good ground in her record, yet her recent form string (100-00) shows inconsistency; 20 days between runs is fine, but she needs everything to go her way from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Surpass And Shine showed he knows how to win when landing a victory five starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 66 marking him out as a genuine threat from stall nine; the concern is four unplaced runs since that success.

runners_data.name: Asdana
runners_data.note: W McCreery yard is 6/19 over 14 days (active barn) and this 4yo filly has a sim-going placed run at 5f/HEA — drop back to Good may be the key and Sam Coen's 5lb claim is attractive, but a true hold-up style in a big field is a structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of nineteen on our rating with a speed figure of 79 that sets her apart from most rivals, Asdana has run over today's trip and going and carries a manageable 141 lb from stall seven, though her recent winless run of five starts — including a pair of unplaced efforts — and a 90-day absence are the key concerns.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride, which upgrades the profile significantly — the horse has a 5f win on Soft and a placed run at the trip, and Keane's tactical intelligence gives this hold-up type its best chance of finding a gap late.
runners_data.comment: Lethimfly catches the eye as the top-rated runner in the field, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives with course-relevant experience; yet to score in his last five starts, and that winless run of form is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 5f on Good ground (2nd and 4th), with prominent enough cruising speed to sit close to the pace despite a hold-up tendency — Ben Coen aboard for the Murphy yard, who are 2/10 over 14 days, makes this one of the better-placed improvers in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Simmering Seas nonetheless brings solid placed form — second last time out and a second three starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 140 lb from stall 15 are factors to weigh against her.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 5f on Good ground and has three placed efforts from eight similar-going starts — a naturally prominent racer who will likely track Ballysax Lil' Mick directly and is ideally profiled for the shape this race is likely to take.
runners_data.comment: Steel Magnolia won last time out and was second two starts back, giving her a sharp upward curve in form, though a seventh three starts back tempers expectations; experience over today's trip and going helps, but 138 lb from stall 17 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: One Cool Bear
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with headgear (visor) who has been mapped to midfield purely because the field is overcrowded with rear-runners; his actual race-style is off the pace and, at OR=55, he has not placed on Good ground in 14 attempts — the redistribution compounds an already difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and returning after 85 days off, One Cool Bear faces questions about fitness, yet he has run over today's distance and going before and carries 137 lb from stall three, with our rating of 62 suggesting he holds a little more in reserve than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type running just five days ago, shown in midfield on the map simply because the field cannot accommodate all rear-runners in their natural position — however, he won at 6f on Good and has sound placed form, and if he settles mid-pack in running he could be live late.
runners_data.comment: Glen Breeze won four starts back but has posted a sixth, fifth and ninth in his last three outings, suggesting he may be hard to catch right now; he has run over today's trip and going before, though the quick five-day turnaround is a concern.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: A consistent back-of-the-field runner who has failed to place in 10 Good-ground outings, and whose natural running style means he is mapped forward as a redistribution artefact rather than a genuine midfield horse — the race shape here does not suit him.
runners_data.comment: Caffu Zafeen has run over today's trip and going, yet he has been winless in his last five starts with a best recent effort of ninth, and 132 lb from stall 19 makes things no easier for a gelding rated 49 on official figures.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra Dream
runners_data.note: 239 days off the track, only three career runs (all on Standard), and flagged as a fader in the finish — the combination of absence, unfamiliar surface, and tactical weakness makes this a very difficult task on debut for the stable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and absent for 239 days, Cleopatra Dream faces a stiff task on these figures as the 15th-ranked of 19 runners, though she has run over today's trip and carries a clear weight.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fade finisher with a hold-up style, yet shown in midfield only because the field forced redistribution — the yard (Thornton, 1/3 over 14 days) has some recent activity, but a 50-day break and a tendency to weaken late are negatives in this sprint.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Monastere faces a stiff task returning from 50 days off and after finishing ninth last time out, though he has experience of today's trip and conditions and did score three starts back.

runners_data.name: Ballysax Lil' Mick
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the single horse who will set the race's tactical shape — at OR=43 and with a 5f Good win in the last five runs, he is not here to be competitive for the prize but his ability to get to the front unchallenged is the most important piece of the pace puzzle.
runners_data.comment: Ballysax Lil' Mick has run over today's trip and going before, and 20 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but he is winless in his last five starts and his official mark of 43 makes the task look stiff from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with an outstanding 14/15 starts on Good ground record and two wins at this course and distance — a prominent racer trained by Timmons who will press Ballysax Lil' Mick and represents the most consistent course-and-distance profile in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 14th of 19 on our figures, Step Back In Time faces a stiff task here; a third two starts back offers the slender consolation, and she has run over today's trip and going before, returning on a quick 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Kidd
runners_data.note: Only three career runs with a best of 7th, flagged as a fader, and held up from the back — a 49-day break does not improve the picture for a lightly raced 3yo who has never suggested a 19-runner 5f handicap is within reach.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kidd faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going, and a 49-day break at least means she arrives fresh, but her recent unplaced efforts make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: The Love Machine
runners_data.note: Held up in a narrow back-of-field style and placed in midfield on the map as a redistribution, not because he runs there naturally — the best recent run was a 5th of 6 on Soft, and this Good-ground sprint at 5f looks sharp for a horse who typically wants further.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, The Love Machine does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his 31-day break gives connections time to have him spot-on; 124 lb from stall 18 make it hard to fancy him strongly, however.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Placed five times in recent runs (mostly 5-6f on Good) and runs prominently enough to be a consistent finisher in the top five — no wins from 15 similar-going starts is the caution, but the Rory Cleary booking for the Lynch yard adds a small positive tick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Jackandthefox is hard to fancy despite the fitness edge of a 33-day break; he has run over today's trip and going before, but consistent near-miss finishes without threatening suggest improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Lismacbryan
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader and most recently 19th of 19 on Good ground — runs for a yard with zero recent winners (0/2 T14), and being mapped to midfield masks what is genuinely a hold-up profile in a race where late cover will be near impossible to find in a 19-horse sprint.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Lismacbryan is hard to fancy on recent form, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a handy 13-day turnaround from draw 1.

races.paceDynamic: Ballysax Lil' Mick is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to press from the outside, should be able to roll to the lead unchallenged from the gate and set a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground over Navan's straight 5f. Step Back In Time and Rosato are the most natural prominent types and will look to slot in just off the leader, giving the race a single-file, processional shape rather than a truly contested pace. With the gallop measured rather than frantic, the prime real estate will be the first two or three lengths off the leader — horses that can track without burning energy and then quicken from a handy position are structurally favoured over deep hold-up types who will need a gap that a 19-runner field may not provide. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and short-striding hold-up types who can position themselves close to the pace — Steel Magnolia and Simmering Seas are exactly the profile this shape rewards. This field carries a substantial cluster of true hold-up horses: One Cool Bear, Glen Breeze, Caffu Zafeen, Monastere, The Love Machine, and Lismacbryan are all genuine off-the-pace types who are unlikely to secure their natural rear position and have been mapped forward by necessity — among them, Glen Breeze and One Cool Bear are most likely to actually find cover near the rear of midfield, but none can bank on clear running late in a 19-runner sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick leads at a sustainable tempo and the race is strung out in single file, allowing prominent trackers to take over inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Steel Magnolia's recent 5f Good-ground win and prominent style make her the textbook beneficiary of a race run to suit her; Simmering Seas, with two placed efforts at 5f on Good, has the natural cruising speed to pounce from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick goes off too fast in front of 19 runners and ties up in the final 100 yards, opening the door for late challengers.
scenarios.body: A faster early pace would compress the field and create the gap late finishers need through a packed 5f sprint field; Simmering Seas, with genuine form at 2/5f/GOO, has the late kick to capitalise if the pace blows up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos Off Slow Pace, Wide
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace and large field cause serious crowding in mid-race and several prominent types get shuffled wide, handing an advantage to horses who draw a clean line.
scenarios.body: Step Back In Time's consistent course-and-distance profile (14/15 starts on Good ground) and prominent style give it the best chance of threading through if the field fans wide; Jackandthefox, placed five times at this trip, could benefit from clear daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick gets an even softer lead than expected and the prominent horses fail to mount a coordinated challenge, leaving the leader in front longer than the pace map suggests.
scenarios.body: At OR=43 and 8 years old this is a low-percentage outcome, but the absence of any horse willing to pressure from the outside means the scenario cannot be ruled out entirely; Step Back In Time would be the most likely horse to close the gap and threaten.

watchPoints.text: Steel Magnolia tracked the pace to win last time at 5f on Good — watch her in behind Ballysax Lil' Mick from the jump, as any hesitation in the draw could cost her the prominent position this race shape requires.

Step Back In Time has the most consistent Good-ground record in the race at 14/15 and will challenge for the lead from the off — if he forces Ballysax Lil' Mick to quicken sooner than expected, the whole pace map changes and closers gain ground.

With 19 runners over a straight 5f on Good ground, a significant traffic incident in the first furlong is very possible — horses drawn wide (particularly those naturally at the rear who cannot get back) are at real risk of being buried early and never recovering.

Lethimfly is partnered by Colin Keane, who is capable of manufacturing a run from a hold-up position that no other jockey in this field could engineer — monitor his positioning from the start as an indicator of whether the hold-up profile has any realistic chance today.

Simmering Seas has run seven days ago and the Murphy yard is 2/10 over 14 days — a second quick run on identical Good ground over the same trip she was placed at recently makes her one of the more interesting drifters to watch in the market.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has finished second twice over this course-and-distance on Good ground in recent weeks, suggesting healthy form, but a 7lb claimer riding adds uncertainty and the horse has zero wins from 15 runs on similar going — placed money is easier to find than winning money here.
runners_data.comment: Erosandpsyche ran second last time out and is back quickly on six days' rest, which speaks to his wellbeing, and he has run over today's trip and going before; yet to win in recent starts, but drawn four carrying 140 lb, his overall profile makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Thunderbear
runners_data.note: Returns from a 77-day break wearing a tongue plate having last won over 6f on Good ground; the step back to 5f is a question, the layoff is another, and trainer Stephen Thorne has struck with none of his last three runners, though a genuinely fresh horse is not always a negative over a sharp trip.
runners_data.comment: Thunderbear warrants plenty of respect — rated 103 and ranked top of the field here, he has a win in his last five starts and brings both distance and going experience to the table, though his two most recent unplaced efforts and a 77-day absence are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Amiata
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for the in-form G M Lyons yard (5 winners from 26 runners over 14 days) on a three-year-old who has won four of 15 on similar going; sits in a midfield map slot because the field's hold-up contingent is overcrowded at the rear, meaning Keane will need to find a more forward pitch than the horse's natural style suggests — that positional compromise slightly undermines what is otherwise a strong form profile.
runners_data.comment: Amiata arrives on the back of a win nine days ago and has won three times in his last six starts, showing a reliable winning thread; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 130 lb is the one factor that could blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with seven placed finishes from 13 runs on similar ground under Ben Coen, and has finished in the first four in each of his last five starts over 5f; ideally positioned to press Allsortz from the off and should be prominent throughout, making this race shape almost tailor-made for his profile.
runners_data.comment: Placed on each of his last two starts, with a win four starts back giving his recent form a solid foundation, Namiid has experience of today's trip and conditions and his 86 rating suggests he holds clear claims; the 49-day absence is the one thing to take on trust.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner over a distance where solo leaders on Good ground can dictate; has form figures of 7-11 in recent 5f Good starts yet owns a win over the trip in softer conditions — the risk is that its natural position sets the pace others key off rather than guaranteeing the win itself.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partner has finished outside the first six in each of its last four 5f/6f Good ground starts, form figures reading 9-9-7-9; the tongue tie and breast girth are familiar headgear and the trainer has no recent winners, making it hard to construct an optimistic case without a substantial improvement in form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Moltophino at least showed encouragement with a runner-up finish last time out, 14 days ago, and he has run over today's distance and going before; carrying 119 lb from stall eight, a rating of 83 suggests he retains ability, though consistency remains the question.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Won twice over 6f on Good ground in recent form and ran second two starts ago, so the raw ability is there; however, this is a natural hold-up horse being mapped into midfield because the field's rear is overcrowded, and over a sharp 5f at Navan with a single front-runner setting a steady tempo, the race may simply be over before Siobhan Rutledge can deliver a challenge from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and returning just three days after his last outing, Gotta Catch'em All faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and showed a third two starts back among recent form that also includes a couple of wins.

runners_data.name: Dandyville
runners_data.note: Form figures of 0-0-0-0-0 across the last five starts with positional finishes in double figures in each — the redistribution into midfield reflects race-shape congestion but is almost a moot point given that the horse has shown no indication of competitiveness at this level regardless of where it maps.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Dandyville is hard to fancy despite returning quickly just three days ago; he has run over today's distance and going before, and stall three is his draw.

races.paceDynamic: Allsortz is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Navan handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to push against, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable rhythm rather than a scorching gallop. Namiid and Moltophino will press from prominent positions just off the leader, meaning the front two furlongs will be honest but not frenetic on Good ground. The moderate, controlled tempo this shape produces tends to reward horses that travel well into the race without burning energy early — prominent and handy types get a soft lead to track and can sprint from two furlongs out, while true hold-up horses risk being left with too little time to close. Three genuine hold-up types — Amiata, Gotta Catch'em All and Dandyville — are pushed into midfield on the map because this field holds more come-from-behind runners than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear, and Amiata (Colin Keane, in-form Lyons yard) is best placed of those three to secure a workable midfield pitch, while Dandyville's dire recent form makes it the least likely to feature regardless of positioning. This race shape firmly favours horses racing prominently or tracking the pace at the head of midfield — those who can hold a handy position and quicken over the final furlong will have the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Allsortz controls, proximity wins
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz gets a clean lead and sets a sustainable but honest pace, allowing prominent horses to draft close.
scenarios.body: Namiid and Moltophino track the leader inside the final two furlongs and the race becomes a sprint between those who have been handy throughout; the Good ground rewards quick, balanced horses over the final 100 yards rather than late-chargers. Horses closest to the pace at the two-furlong pole are best served and the hold-up contingent simply has insufficient ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, closers sneak
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz goes off too fast for its own comfort and weakens sharply inside the final furlong, opening a gap for those held up.
scenarios.body: The leader's recent form shows inconsistency over 5f on Good ground and a flattening out in the closing stages would compress the field, giving midfield runners a route through; Amiata's course-and-distance winning form under Colin Keane makes it the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace duel tightens race
scenarios.trigger: If Namiid or Moltophino applies pressure to Allsortz earlier than expected, lifting the tempo and setting up a truly run race.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated pace would stretch the field and tire the front pair, bringing the hold-up horses into contention from further back; Erosandpsyche has twice finished second over 5f Good at a similar level and could be the horse to benefit most with cover through the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, field bunches wide
scenarios.trigger: If trouble in running or a slow break disrupts the race shape and the field races in a tight pack to the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically messy 5f sprint on Good ground would produce a blanket finish where positional advantages are neutralised; Thunderbear, fresh off 77 days and carrying a tongue tie, would be least disadvantaged by a changed race shape given its hold-up style, though its return from a long layoff is a clear concern.

watchPoints.text: Namiid's early positioning will be critical — if Ben Coen gets him slotted directly behind Allsortz in the first furlong he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given his pattern of tracking the pace and finishing strongly over 5f Good ground.

Amiata's Colin Keane booking suggests market confidence, but watch whether Keane drops the horse in midfield or attempts to push forward from the stalls — if he can secure a pitch closer to the pace than the horse's natural style demands, the Lyons runner upgrades significantly as a threat.

Allsortz's early gallop tempo is the axis on which the entire race turns — if the leader's sectionals appear slow in the first two furlongs, the race sets up for the prominent horses and hold-up types alike, removing the tactical edge the lone front-runner might otherwise hold.

Thunderbear's 77-day absence is worth monitoring in the betting market: if money arrives for the Thorne runner it may signal stable confidence that the horse is fit and ready to go first time up, which would make a reoccurrence of its 1/6f Good win more plausible.

Dandyville's recent form (five consecutive zeros, all finishing deep in the field) makes it a race-reading tool rather than a betting one — if it somehow leads or races prominently it would signal a truly unusual pace dynamic that would invalidate the standard race-shape read.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Return Of The Jumps At Navan Racecourse September 19th Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Albatala
runners_data.note: Has won at 10f on soft and placed at 1m2f on good, making this trip and ground combination viable; natural prominent runner for Sam Coen, ideally suited to tracking a single front-runner and getting first run.|
runners_data.comment: Albatala won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a balanced profile, though 55 days off the track introduces a fitness query and she faces 23 rivals carrying 142 lb from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: True hold-up specialist, age nine with 12 qualifying runs at this going band and one place; trainer Adrian Sexton has had no winners in the past 14 days, and only 10 days since last run leaves little scope for significant improvement.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Katherine arrives here on a quick ten-day turnaround carrying 142 lb from stall one, and while she has run over today's trip before, her recent string of unplaced efforts makes improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Pallatine Hills
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type from Eddie & Patrick Harty whose recent history is over 8-9f, so this 1m2f trip is a step up; placed once in nine similar-going runs, and the distance question is the dominant concern here.|
runners_data.comment: Pallatine Hills brings strong claims here, ranked second of 24 on our rating with a speed figure of 76 to his name, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that he is winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up runner from P Sweeney with a sole win over this going band from 15 qualifying starts; has been running over shorter trips (7-8f) recently, making this 1m2f a test of stamina he hasn't consistently demonstrated.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, God Knows nonetheless carries a rating of 77 — top of 24 runners — and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going to call on; she maps as the one to beat despite her recent struggles.

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on good ground under W J Lee for McCreery, who has been in good form (6 from 19 over 14 days); its natural hold-up style means it will likely find itself further forward than ideal given the redistribution — STYLE_FIT tempers expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Make The Tide rates 62 on our figures, fourth-best of these, and bounced back to score last time out, giving her strong claims fresh from just three days ago; the main concern is whether that quick turnaround blunts her finishing effort here.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell runner on a 73-day break, yet has a solid good-ground second over 10f and genuinely operates as a hold-up horse; the long absence is the main risk, but this is a true closer whose profile fits a late run in a compressed straight.|
runners_data.comment: Neon Eyes shaped with promise when a close second two starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going in her favour, but a 73-day absence combined with a trainer hitting only 5% in the last 14 days makes confidence harder to hold.

runners_data.name: African Affair
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Ms Sheila Lavery returning after 110 days off; only three career starts, all on good or soft, and the fade tendency flagged in finish makes a big field over 1m2f a daunting assignment for this lightly-raced filly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and absent for 110 days, African Affair arrives short of recent encouragement, though he has run over today's distance and going before and carries a manageable 133 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with four places from 15 similar-going runs, including a win and a second at 8f; mapped to midfield rather than the rear due to field overcrowding, which slightly compromises its natural finishing position — form is honest though.|
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and a winner six starts back, Alto Sax brings distance and going experience to the table and his our rating edges above his official mark, but that ninth two starts back is a concern and 133 lb is no featherweight ask.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer who carries a fade-in-finish flag, making this 1m2f stamina test a real concern; has placed once in 15 good-ground runs and has recent form over longer trips, but the pattern of emptying late is a consistent worry.|
runners_data.comment: Jazz Forever has run over today's trip and going before, but winless in his last six starts with three consecutive unplaced efforts weighing against him; third four starts back offers some encouragement, and at 133 lb from stall three he has conditions to work with.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and therefore guaranteed to lead — Shane Foley for KJ Condon, five qualifying runs at this trip on good ground and consistently mid-table finishes suggest she stays but does not accelerate; her value is in controlling the tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Mare Crisium has nonetheless shown consistency with a pair of fourths in recent outings and has experience of today's trip and conditions; 133 lb from stall 14 is the challenge as she tries to edge forward from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Two wins in 14 good-ground runs (including over 8f and 10f) for Michael Mulvany, with Terry Casey (7) booked; a hold-up type whose record of two wins and two places in similar going makes it among the better-credentialed closers in this field at the distance.|
runners_data.comment: Nephin Mountain won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but carrying 133 lb from stall 19 and an official rating of 57 with patchy recent form — two wins and three disappointing efforts in his last six starts — suggests he is not without risks.

runners_data.name: Wipeawayyourtears
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good ground and placed twice in eight similar-going runs — genuine stamina and course-relevant form; hold-up style is honest but the five-day turnaround and blinkered headgear suggest connections are searching for more consistency.|
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and filled the frame twice in recent starts, but she comes into this unplaced last time out, just five days on, and a high weight of 133 lb from stall 23 tests her stamina in a competitive 24-runner field.

runners_data.name: Calamint
runners_data.note: Six-year-old true hold-up type from Adrian Murray, placed in three of 15 similar-going runs with a win over 10f on heavy; mapped to midfield through redistribution yet operates naturally from off the pace — holds solid each-way claims if getting an unimpeded passage.|

runners_data.name: Oh I Do Declare
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning after 143 days on a sparse profile of three runs, all on soft or heavy — the good ground here is untested for this horse; the natural inclination to race hold-up combined with redistribution and the fade flag makes this one of the more vulnerable runners.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, the most recent of which came 143 days ago, Oh I Do Declare heads into this off the back of a ninth and two unplaced efforts, and our rating of 48 ranks him 19th of 24 — though he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: A horse whose five recent runs all ended in mid-to-rear finishes on good ground, and the fade tendency is a consistent feature of its races; hold-up type pushed into midfield by redistribution, with zero wins or places from five comparable starts.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 20th of 24 on our figures, Chloe's Boy faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a consistent pattern of mid-pack finishes in a narrow OR band — all five recent runs resulted in positions between eighth and sixteenth; the fade flag, good-ground-only form, and redistribution from the rear all combine to limit expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kingcharles has struggled for consistency, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround from stall five carrying 129 lb; our rating of 58 suggests a shade more ability than his official mark of 53 implies.

runners_data.name: Churchill Gale
runners_data.note: Returning from 304 days off for Dermot McLoughlin, with the last qualifying run over 10f on good; four placing-free runs in similar going since a mid-field effort — the long absence is the overriding concern and the horse will need to strip fitter.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for over 300 days, Churchill Gale faces a stiff task from stall 20 carrying 126 lb, and her finishing positions offer little encouragement — though she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: De Songbird
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from TG McCourt whose recent profile is all on 6-10f trips, making this 1m2f a clear step into unknown territory; seven runs without a win and a pattern of finishing in mid-to-lower positions, with redistribution placing it further forward than its natural station.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, De Songbird has struggled for consistency, though she has run over today's distance and going before and comes here on a sharp 14-day turnaround; carrying 125 lb from stall 11, she remains one to watch rather than follow blindly at this stage.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 8f on good ground and placed three times, giving a solid record; a genuine hold-up type in a trainer yard (Mulvany) among the more active stables, though at a short (6-day) turnaround and bumped forward from its natural rear position by redistribution.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18th of 24 on our figures, Cause I Like You faces a stiff task on these ratings, though she was a winner three starts back and filled the runner-up spot last time out, suggesting some residual form to cling to; the return after just six days is the main query.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with five runs all producing double-figure finishes on good ground, and the fade tendency is flagged; redistribution moves this hold-up type toward midfield, and with zero wins or places across similar conditions, the bar for optimism is high.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Miss Ivor faces a stiff task here; she does return on a short turnaround with going experience in her favour, but her recent string of unplaced efforts makes it hard to fancy her chances.

runners_data.name: Capall Cuain
runners_data.note: Only three runs to date, all resulting in 13th or worse on good ground; a hold-up type with a fade warning who is stepped up considerably in trip from 7-8f, and the combination of inexperience, redistribution, and the stamina question makes this a very difficult race.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Capall Cuain faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's going before and 18 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning 11 days after a 0 finish, with a career record of zero wins and no places from seven comparable starts; the fade flag, redistribution, and modest recent form over varying trips make this one for spectators rather than shortlisters.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 23 of 24 on our figures, Bang Po faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a relatively quick turnaround of 11 days, but little else in his recent profile invites confidence.

runners_data.name: Haeret In Pectore
runners_data.note: Five-year-old back after 125 days, with form primarily on standard and soft ground over 7-10f — the good ground here is noted and the trip is an extension; redistribution places this hold-up type in midfield, and the absence combined with uncertain going preference makes assessing it difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 22 of 24 on our figures, Haeret In Pectore arrives 125 days between runs and faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and retains a featherweight 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with one win in 15 good-ground runs over distances up to 13f and two further places; hold-up type carried into midfield by redistribution, with a Reserve 3 jockey booking and only three days since last run — trainer Sean Davis has no recent winners in the 14-day window.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and back just three days after his most recent unplaced effort, Giselles Defence faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 61 offers a sliver of encouragement from stall 15 carrying 134 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Mare Crisium is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 24-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to press her — with no other confirmed leader, she will stride to the front from her draw and control fractions entirely on her own terms over this 1m2f trip on Good ground. The pace she sets will therefore be sustainable rather than frenetic, creating a steadily-run race that is unlikely to burn off horses with stamina and will reward those who can track the leader without covering extra ground. Horses such as Oh I Do Declare, Make The Tide, Kingcharles, Churchill Gale, and several other nominally hold-up types have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the sheer volume of hold-up runners in this field means they cannot all settle at the rear — the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent position behind Mare Crisium are Albatala and Jazz Forever, who are natural prominent racers, alongside Nephin Mountain and Wipeawayyourtears who have the tactical speed to slot in. With a single uncontested leader dictating a measured gallop, the race shape strongly favours prominent/midfield closers with genuine stamina for 1m2f who can track the pace and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out rather than a single explosive burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium dictates unchallenged fractions and the large field compresses behind, enabling her or a close tracker to outsay rivals in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Mare Crisium sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop that suits her proven front-running profile, and horses tracking her closely through the race get first run in the straight without burning extra energy weaving through a field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely steady and horses racing prominently in second to fifth position produce sustained runs down the straight.
scenarios.body: Albatala and Jazz Forever, tracking the leader from the front rank, are ideally placed to capitalise as the field concertinas in the final two furlongs without needing to find gaps.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the sustained pace is just quick enough to string out the field and create a proper run from mid-division in the straight.
scenarios.body: Neon Eyes and Alto Sax, genuine hold-up types who kept their natural position, would appreciate any increase in tempo that rewards a sweeping finish; Calamint also fits this profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 24-runner field causes significant bunching, interference in the straight, or a false pace that scrambles the finish entirely.
scenarios.body: In a rough race with little early order, resolute stayers who avoid trouble and keep a straight line home benefit most; Wipeawayyourtears and Nephin Mountain, with proven good-ground form at the trip, could emerge from the scrimmage.

watchPoints.text: Mare Crisium under Shane Foley is the sole front-runner in a 24-runner field and could easily get a soft, uncontested lead — if the pace she sets is slower than expected, horses tracking her closely risk getting trapped on the rail through the final bend.

The field of 24 contains an extreme excess of hold-up types, meaning horses like Make The Tide, Oh I Do Declare, Churchill Gale, and Kingcharles will be forced to race several lengths forward of their natural position — watch for midfield bunching and interference as these horses fail to settle where they want.

Neon Eyes is returning from a 73-day break for Gavin Cromwell — it has the cleanest hold-up profile in the field and genuine placed form on good ground at 10f, but fitness off a break in a 24-runner handicap is a live risk if it needs a race to come to itself.

Nephin Mountain and Cause I Like You are both trained by Michael Mulvany, who has had one winner from 13 runners in the past 14 days — stable form is quietly ticking over and both horses have legitimate good-ground credentials, so Mulvany's tactical instructions between the pair are worth noting at the off.

Wipeawayyourtears runs only five days after its last outing and carries blinkered headgear — the quick turnaround combined with a hood suggests the stable is chasing something specific, and it has won over 1m2f on good ground before; the short break is unusual and worth monitoring in the paddock.

races.name: Return Of The Jumps At Navan Racecourse September 19th Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner in this 24-runner field; OR 58, Good-ground form reads well across recent starts (3-1-2 in last five), and Paul Flynn's runner is fit off a 20-day break — the key question is whether a blinkers-wearing six-year-old can hold on from the front against a late charge, though with no genuine pace rival to push him, the answer could easily be yes.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner four starts back, Nibras Rainbow has shown he can compete at this level, but a ninth two starts back tempers enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, and 142 lb is no small ask from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on this Peter Fahey hold-up mare, who is sharp off just a 9-day turnaround; her best form in similar going came at 12f and she may find 10f on the quick side here, with no sim-going wins in 11 attempts adding a quiet concern.
runners_data.comment: Placed third three starts back and second five starts back, Miss Crinshawn arrives here quickly on nine days' rest with experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 60 ranks her among the chief dangers in a 24-runner field; the risk is that she remains winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Ballaghkeen
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's three-year-old returns after a 323-day absence — a significant layoff flag — and while the T14 strike rate of 2/7 suggests the yard has runners ready, his form ceiling at 7-8f on his last runs makes this step to 10f on return speculative at best.
runners_data.comment: Ballaghkeen is yet to score in her last four starts and returns after a 323-day absence, which is a significant unknown, though she has run over today's going before and carries a manageable 138 lb from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Keilah
runners_data.note: A six-year-old hold-up type whose sim-going record shows 13 placed efforts from 15, suggesting a horse that consistently fills places without winning; the tongue-tie and cheekpieces are in play, and a trip back to 10f (best runs have come at this trip) is a small positive.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's three-year-old is a consistent placer with four seconds from ten runs on Good ground and arrives sharp off nine days; a genuine stay-on type whose 14f second on Good is encouraging for this 10f test, and Rory Mulligan claims 5lb off the top.
runners_data.comment: Millhone has been a model of consistency, placing in four of her last six starts with a second last time out and a third two starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going holds her in good stead; the main concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Has a "fades in finish" flag and is a true hold-up type whose natural rear-of-field position is squeezed by the density of closers in this field — in a race likely run at a controlled pace, there is little reason to expect Nicola Burns can generate the momentum needed to land a blow from the back.

runners_data.name: Strike De Vega
runners_data.note: Recent form reads 0-6-0-0, and the "fades in finish" flag is a serious concern for Gary Carroll's mount; distance form at 14f and 10f on Good is uninspiring, and this is a horse asking questions rather than providing answers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 18th of 24 on our figures, Strike De Vega faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Queen Leila
runners_data.note: All five sim-going runs have come on Soft or AW at the Curragh rather than Good, so the going profile is not as encouraging as the OK tag suggests; Luke McAteer rides a three-year-old whose one win came at 8f on Soft/AW, making the 10f on Good an untested combination.
runners_data.comment: Showed she can win when scoring two starts back, but has since disappointed, finishing unplaced last time out; has run over today's going before and returns after 21 days, though her official mark of 55 suggests she faces a stiff task from the field.

runners_data.name: Tickle The Cat
runners_data.note: Has the "fades in finish" flag and all four career runs have produced finishes of 7th, 11th, 8th and 11th — there is no evidence here of a horse about to find improvement, and Chris Hayes cannot manufacture ability that isn't there.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 19th of 24 on our figures, Tickle The Cat faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: A true hold-up operator whose place in the midfield map is a product of the overcrowded rear; Seamie Heffernan's mount has zero wins and zero places on Good in 15 attempts at similar going, which is as damning a stat as exists in this field — the sim-going record (5/15) is not encouragement, it is a warning.
runners_data.comment: Trishuli River tops our ratings in a wide-open field and has experience of today's trip and conditions, yet her recent string of unplaced efforts — including eighth last time out, 47 days ago — is the obvious concern for a mare still winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on Noel Meade's three-year-old, who has been off 63 days and carries the "fades in finish" flag; genuinely a hold-up horse pushed forward on the map by the field's back-heavy makeup, and with five runs at this trip on Good all resulting in 5th or worse, the raw evidence does not invite confidence.
runners_data.comment: Captain Con is winless in his last five starts and returns after 63 days off with a trainer who has yet to land a winner from 24 runners in the past fortnight, making it hard to fancy his claims despite having run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Thegooseiscooked
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran with one win in 15 similar-going starts; Jack Kearney claims 3lb and the horse has shown flickers of form at 10f on Good but is fundamentally another rear-group type fighting for the same late ground as a dozen others.
runners_data.comment: Thegooseiscooked has run over today's trip and going, but she arrives winless in her last five starts, with only a third two runs back to show, and 129 lb from stall 19 adds further burden to a mare who will need to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old off 22 days, no win in 15 similar-going runs, and the "fades in finish" flag is entirely consistent with a horse that simply cannot sustain effort in the closing stages; W McCreery's T14 of 6/19 is the yard's best angle here but the horse's own form doesn't support optimism.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Morning Approach has run over today's trip and going before, and 22 days between runs suggests she comes here reasonably fresh; however, a sequence of unplaced efforts makes improvement hard to identify at a rating of 44.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: One of only three genuine prominent types in the field alongside the leader; Terry Casey claims 7lb on Michael Mulvany's three-year-old who is tight off nine days, and a 2nd over 10f on Good in his last five means he has the distance profile — tracking Nibras Rainbow closely is a realistic and potentially winning tactic.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Borora Aura arrives on a quick nine-day turnaround and has run over today's trip and going, though an unplaced effort last time and a run-of-the-mill rating of 49 suggest she faces a stiff task from stall 11 carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: He Knows When
runners_data.note: Returning from 784 days off the track — a layoff that demands extreme caution regardless of any other angle; his form before the break showed consistent prominent running and 10f on Good suited, but a two-year-plus absence makes him an enormous unknown quantity, and Robbie Colgan must somehow find his rhythm immediately.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a lengthy 784-day absence, He Knows When faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a third two starts back offers a hint of ability.

runners_data.name: Emily's Boy
runners_data.note: Has the "fades in finish" flag and all career runs have been on Soft, Heavy or AW — no Good-ground evidence at all, so the going profile is genuinely unknown despite the OK tag; the 147-day break and a horse that naturally closes from the rear in a pace-starved race makes this a very low-probability runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Emily's Boy has been off the track for 147 days and, ranked last on our figures, makes little appeal on these terms despite carrying 125 lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: The blinkers are on for Patrick Magee's three-year-old who is off 21 days; a "fades in finish" tag plus a natural hold-up style mapped forward by necessity — his best run was a 2nd over 13f on Good which suggests a longer trip actually helps, and 10f here may not play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 17th of 24 on our figures, Wingit faces a stiff task here; an unplaced last time does little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's distance and going before and 21 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Sharp off just six days, and Michael Mulvany runs two horses in this race; Wesley Joyce claims 3lb, and while there is a 3rd on Good at 10f in recent history, the "fades in finish" flag and crowded hold-up group membership make it hard to construct a winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Arizona Star has been winless in her last five starts and ranks 20th of 24 on our figures, making her very hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and an eighth last time out at least shows recent racecourse experience.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: All six sim-going runs on Good have produced finishes of 6th, 7th, 8th, 8th, 9th — a remarkably consistent underperformer on the going; the tongue-tie and drop-band headgear combination is tried, and Sean Davis rides, but the form pattern points firmly away.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and carrying 122 lb from stall 23, Due In June faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's going before and a return just six days ago suggests connections are keen.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary picks up the ride on Sheila Lavery's three-year-old who has four consecutive 3rd-4th finishes on Good — a horse that runs to a consistent level without winning; off 24 days and without headgear, she maps to midfield but holds genuine enough form to be considered a place contender if the race runs to suit a grindy, close-up style.
runners_data.comment: Connova has shown consistent form of late, placing third two and three starts back, and returns here on a quick turnaround of 24 days with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour; winless in her last five starts, she maps well on our figures and runs off an official rating of 43.

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse on Jarlath Fahey's three-year-old who has progressive recent form — a 3rd then 6th over 10-12f on Good, suggesting a horse still finding its level; the 43-day gap is manageable and a place claim is not fanciful if traffic permits, though the natural hold-up style is a complication in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well towards the foot of the field on our figures, Cadreville is a tough one to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and at least returns on a feasible 43-day break.

runners_data.name: Sunny Dude
runners_data.note: Has run primarily at 16f on Good with poor results, and this step back to 10f for D Buckley's six-year-old is a dramatic change of pattern; the "fades in finish" flag and 61-day layoff with no confirmed jockey booking compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Sunny Dude has been out of form throughout recent starts, and 61 days off adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 124 lb is manageable, but it is hard to make a case from stall 20.

runners_data.name: Carrickfinn
runners_data.note: All career form has come on Soft or AW — never run on Good going, which makes the going tag here genuinely questionable; the 125-day break and a "fades in finish" flag on a horse with no confirmed jockey making this one of the weakest profiles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Carrickfinn has been consistently out of the frame and returns after 125 days off, making him very hard to fancy here despite having experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Very sharp off just three days — an unusually quick turnaround — and Karl Thornton's three-year-old is a hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map by the weight of numbers; form of 12th-16th-7th-11th-4th
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Onyeisi has managed a fourth five starts back but otherwise largely struggled for form; drawn in stall 15 carrying 130 lb, and back just three days after his latest run, the turnaround gives some pause despite experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Rainbow is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 24-runner field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — with Borora Aura and He Knows When the only other prominent types, neither is likely to hunt Nibras Rainbow hard enough to collapse the fractions. With Good ground over 1m2f at Navan and a sustainable, uncontested gallop, the pace will be honest but controlled, creating a rail-hugging, energy-conserving lead that stretches the field through the early furlongs without burning out the leader. The field is dominated by hold-up horses — Deuteronomy, Captain Con, Onyeisi, Trishuli River and several others are genuine rear-of-field types redistributed into midfield on the map simply because there are far more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the back, and in reality they will all be fighting for the same ground late. This race shape is structurally biased toward horses who can race prominently or in a handy midfield position tracking the controlled pace, as the glut of true hold-up horses will likely find traffic, lack a strong enough pace to sprint off, and face an in-command front-runner who is never asked a serious question until the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nibras Rainbow Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow secures an uncontested lead and the gallop remains controlled throughout, allowing the leader to conserve energy for the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Nibras Rainbow has the run of the race from the front, sets a sustainable tempo on Good ground, and the wall of hold-up horses behind never generates the fierce pace surge needed to reel in a fresh, untroubled leader; Borora Aura and He Knows When, tracking closely, are best positioned to pounce if the leader weakens but may also be outrun to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Movers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough that Nibras Rainbow begins to weaken inside the final furlong, allowing the closest trackers to pick up and go past.
scenarios.body: Borora Aura or He Knows When, racing in a handy position just off the leader, time their move into the straight and sprint clear as the front-runner ties up; this scenario rewards horses that have the stamina to sustain a run from a close-up position rather than needing a wall of pace to launch off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If a fast early pace develops — an unlikely but possible scenario if Borora Aura pushes Nibras Rainbow — creating enough early burn that the closers have a genuine pace to aim at.
scenarios.body: Horses who are true hold-up types get the strong pace they need and sweep through late; however, most of these — Captain Con, Deuteronomy, Trishuli River — carry REDISTRIBUTED tags meaning they are not reliably in position to exploit this and face traffic risks in a 24-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a muddling affair with no real pace injected at any stage and the field compresses through the final bend.
scenarios.body: A steady overall gallop means no positional group is decisively favoured, and a horse with reliable course-distance form who tracks midfield quietly can pick off tiring rivals; this is the least likely outcome given the pace profile clearly points one horse in front.
