runners_data.name: Ben Lomond
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran with a best recent effort of third over 2m, well beaten in all 1m2f starts; trainer Kyne has had no wins from three in 14 days, and though a genuine hold-up type, the redistribution places him forward of his natural ground — this trip looks short of his best distance.

runners_data.name: Deetee
runners_data.note: Returning after a 706-day absence for Lupini, who is 1/8 in the last 14 days; showed placed form in two runs on Good before the layoff and carries prominent-racing credentials that suit this pace scenario, but fitness after nearly two years off is the central question.

runners_data.name: Highlander Addict
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type who has a win to his name over 2m1f on Good, suggesting stamina is his weapon; this 1m2f trip may be a stepping stone but a truly run race would help him, and Flynn's 0/4 in the 14-day window offers little trainer confidence.

runners_data.name: If Not For Grace
runners_data.note: Consistent fader — all three runs on Good have ended in mid-pack or worse finishes, and the fades-in-finish flag reinforces a pattern of not seeing out races; Cusack 0/3 recently, no win or place in three starts, hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins handler is 1/8 in recent fortnight; horse has shown one glimpse of form — second on Heavy at 2m — and is a true hold-up type racing in a field where the back of the race is congested, making its position effectively midfield rather than rear, a compromise that may not suit.

runners_data.name: Medadthebookie
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a repeated finishing pattern of sixth, carrying fades-in-finish flag; all five career runs on Good have ended without a win or place at this trip or beyond, and the 53-day absence adds to the concern.

runners_data.name: Scorcher's Son
runners_data.note: O'Brien handler (9/60 in 14 days) is the key angle for a horse with one run — seventh on Good over 1m — as this step to 1m2f represents the unknown; hold-up style means he depends on a proper pace, which this race shape may not supply.

runners_data.name: Nugentstown Sue
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old mare last seen five days ago, with a career plagued by mid-teen finishes on Good ground and only one placed effort coming at 2m; fades-in-finish flag and repeated poor placed efforts suggest she needs further and a stronger gallop.

runners_data.name: Four Ball
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with two Good-ground runs both producing double-figure finishes; true hold-up horse whose style cannot be accommodated at the back of this field, and the trainer-jockey combination (Murphy/Ryan, 1/12 in 14 days) offers modest support.

runners_data.name: Giordano
runners_data.note: Kilmartin's lone entry in the 14-day window; two runs on Good both finished ninth or worse, and carries the fades-in-finish flag — a true rear-of-field type that the race shape pushes into midfield, which suits neither his style nor his form.

runners_data.name: Gulf Beat
runners_data.note: Debut runner for O'Brien (9/60 in 14 days, elite operator) with no form figures to assess; unknown style mapped as U — the trainer's record in maidens with unexposed three-year-olds demands respect, and any hint of talent could be decisive in a weak field.

runners_data.name: Handani
runners_data.note: Weld's three-year-old is the most consistently placed runner in the field — three placed efforts in three Good-ground starts, including a course-relevant 1m2f effort; prominent style, good jockey (Hayes), and proven form at the trip make him central to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Heriot's Hope
runners_data.note: Debut runner for A. Oliver with no exposed form — style and going unknown; W J Lee is an experienced jockey and Oliver's stable can produce debut winners, but the lack of any form line means this is speculative.

runners_data.name: Legato
runners_data.note: Three-year-old first-timer for Mulvany, 1/13 in 14 days; no form to assess and style listed as unknown — this is a wide-open unknown quantity in a field where established form is thin.

runners_data.name: Metallic
runners_data.note: O'Brien-trained three-year-old with two runs both producing double-figure finishes at 1m2f on Good; fades-in-finish flag and a hold-up style make this difficult to recommend in a steady-pace scenario, despite the powerful yard.

runners_data.name: Michinaga
runners_data.note: Lightly raced for Charles Weld with a sixth and ninth on Good ground; style unknown, trainer 0/8 in 14 days — insufficient evidence to project a pace role, and form figures offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mississippi Shine
runners_data.note: Debut for G M Lyons (5/26 in 14 days, strong strike rate) with Colin Keane taking the ride — the booking of the champion jockey is a meaningful signal for an unexposed three-year-old; unknown style and no form to assess, but trainer-jockey combination elevates this runner's claims significantly.

runners_data.name: Royal Bones
runners_data.note: Harrington-trained (3/31 in 14 days) with a second on Good at 8f and a sixth at 10f; prominent style is perfectly placed to track Camelot Queen and quicken, and the step to 1m2f could unlock stamina that wasn't tested over shorter.

runners_data.name: Steppinoncats
runners_data.note: One run — twelfth on Standard over 7f for Devine (0/6 in 14 days) — provides minimal information; hold-up style and a trainer with no recent form means there is little to recommend this runner in the current race shape.

runners_data.name: Twin Nation
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride for Noel Meade (0/31 in 14 days but an experienced handler) on this debutant; no form to assess and style unknown, though the jockey booking of Heffernan suggests connections are hopeful — worth noting in the unexposed runner group.

runners_data.name: Vico Road
runners_data.note: Debut runner for John Joseph Murphy (0/8 in 14 days) with Gary Carroll aboard; no form or style information available — must be marked as a complete unknown with no specific angle to recommend.

runners_data.name: Camelot Queen
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field, having shown a consistent pattern of placing from the front (three placings in five runs); Wayne Lordan keeps the ride for A P O'Brien (5/31 in 14 days) and the uncontested lead on Good ground at 1m2f gives her a genuine tactical advantage, though her OR of 72 reflects the ceiling of her ability.

runners_data.name: Sakoku
runners_data.note: Murtagh's three-year-old (2/31 in 14 days) showed a noteworthy second at 13f on Good in run two, suggesting stamina; a genuine hold-up type that the crowded rear of this field displaces toward midfield — Ben Coen takes over and the extra furlong compared to previous runs is a positive, making adaptation of role less damaging if the trip brings out improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Camelot Queen is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 23 and, crucially, faces no meaningful pace pressure from another established lead horse — she can roll along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being harried into an injudicious split. With Good ground confirmed throughout the card at Navan over 1m2f, the pace will be honest but not frantic, and a horse in control of the fractions from the front is in an enviable position. The large field of hold-up types behind her creates a genuine tactical problem: Sakoku, Ben Lomond, Giordano, Four Ball, and It's Good To Talk are all natural closers, but with so many of that ilk they will be queued up and reliant on a strong enough gallop to make their late efforts count — and Camelot Queen is unlikely to provide that. This race shape strongly favours prominent-racing types who can track the leader at close range and pounce approaching the final two furlongs, with hold-up horses facing a traffic and pace-dependent disadvantage. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Sakoku, Ben Lomond, and Giordano are among those most likely to be shuffled forward out of their natural position, though Sakoku and Ben Lomond have the class profiles to adapt.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Camelot Queen Controls, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Camelot Queen sets a fair but unhurried pace and prominent trackers cruise into contention turning for home.
scenarios.body: Camelot Queen dictates on a solo lead at a sustainable tempo, and the first horse to quicken off her back from second or third position takes the race before the hold-up closers can wind up their challenges; this shape is the most probable given the lone front-runner dynamic on Good ground. Handani and Royal Bones, with proven form tracking pace in similar conditions, are ideally suited to fire into the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutants Land Blind
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced or debut runners — Mississippi Shine, Gulf Beat, Heriot's Hope, or Twin Nation — produces a performance that outclasses the exposed handicappers.
scenarios.body: A well-bred, unexposed runner with an elite trainer (Lyons, O'Brien, Meade, Oliver) drops into a weak maiden field and finds that Good ground and a steady pace allows their natural class to dominate without needing a specific race shape; these are runners with unknown ceilings. The prominent-to-midfield profile suits a horse with engine to spare — Mississippi Shine (Colin Keane booked) and Twin Nation (Seamie Heffernan) are most dangerous here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swarm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Camelot Queen sets a genuine pace that stretches the field, giving true hold-up horses a real target to run at.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly strong early gallop strings out the field, and the closers get a proper pace to aim at, allowing Sakoku or Highlander Addict to come from behind and reel in tired rivals in the final furlong. This scenario is discounted because Camelot Queen is uncontested and has every incentive to conserve, making a strong true-pace finish less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Held Up Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo collapses into a crawl, the field bunches, and the race turns into a sprint finish that scrambles all running styles.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace creates a mass finish from the home turn, with position and luck in running determining the outcome rather than ability or style; this lottery scenario advantages any horse in a clean position at the right moment. Handani's consistent placed form and Sakoku's tactical versatility make them dangers even in a messy finish, though no hold-up horse is guaranteed a clean run in a 23-runner bunch sprint.

watchPoints.text: Camelot Queen's early tempo will dictate everything — if she quickens out smartly from the wide 23-runner draw and gets a clear lead, the gap between her and the prominent trackers will define whether this race is winnable from the front or not; watch how quickly she establishes her position in the opening two furlongs.

Mississippi Shine, Gulf Beat, Twin Nation and Heriot's Hope are all debutants from powerful yards with top-tier jockeys booked (Keane, Heffernan, Lee, Sheridan) — any one of them could be a well-prepared first-timer in a field of exposed maidens, and their unknown ability is the largest single uncertainty in the race.
